newsitem.title: USA: Avg equity fund falls 1.98 pct in Q1 - Lipper.
newsitem.headline: Avg equity fund falls 1.98 pct in Q1 - Lipper.

text.p: The average U.S. general equity fund fell 1.98 percent in the first fiscal quarter, the first negative period since the fourth quarter of 1994, according to Lipper Analytical Services.
Lipper said in a statement that "concerns over rapid economic growth and higher interest rates began to affect the investing climate."

Lipper said domestic equity funds have been declining since at least late January. "The volatility that marked the last weeks of the quarter may signal a change in the market's overall direction," said Michael Lipper, the firm's president.
The average science and technology fund dropped 8.60 percent in the quarter, although the sector was up 7.61 percent for the past 12 months.
Other equity sectors posted gains: Index funds rose 2.52 percent, and conservative equity income funds edged up 1.68 percent.
Japanese funds dropped 6.70 percent, and Canadian funds fell 6.59 percent.
Other overseas funds prospered, according to Lipper. Latin American funds rose 13.68 percent, while the average emerging market fund gained 9.57 percent.
"This rate of progress is unlikely to continue," Lipper said.

The top five funds for the quarter were: American Heritage, up 48.21 percent; Lexington Troika Russia, up 46 percent; Merrill Middle East Africa, up 23.13 percent; Rembrandt Latin American Equity, up 17.29 percent; and Vontobel Eastern European, up 16.52 percent.

According to Lipper, the worst laggards included Calvert Strategic Growth, off 26.15 percent; Parkstone Small Cap Institutional, off 23.13 percent; PBHG Core Growth, off 22.14 percent; TCW/Dean Witter Small Cap Growth, off 21.22 percent; and TCW/Dean Witter Mid-Cap Equity, off 21.17 percent.
